title: Lines from a little book
translation: I once read a little book called Ichigon Hōdan, a collection of things said by holy men of the past. These are the ones that stayed with me.
When you can't decide whether to do something or not, it's usually better not to.
If you care about the next life, don't own so much as a pickle jar. Not even a good copy of the sutras or a fine statue of the Buddha. Owning good things is pointless.
If you have left the world, the best way to live is to arrange things so that you don't miss what you don't have.
The high-born should become low, the wise foolish, the rich poor, and the talented useless.
Following the Buddha's path comes down to this: have time on your hands and keep the world's business off your mind. That comes first.
There were others too, but I don't remember them.
original: たふとき{聖|ひじり}のいひおきけることを{書|か}きつけて、{一言芳談|いちごんはうだん}とかや{名|な}づけたる{草紙|さうし}を{見|み}{侍|はべ}りしに、{心|こころ}に{会|あ}ひて{覚|おぼ}えし{事|こと}ども。
{一|ひとつ}{為|し}やせまし、{為|せ}ずやあらましと{思|おも}ふことは、おほやう{為|せ}ぬはよきなり。
{一|ひとつ}{後世|ごせ}を{思|おも}はむものは、{糂汰|じんだ}{瓶|がめ}{一|ひと}つも{持|も}つまじきことなり。
{持経|ぢきやう}、{本尊|ほぞん}にいたるまで、よき{物|もの}を{持|も}つ、よしなきことなり。
{一|ひとつ}{遁世者|とんせいしや}は、なきに{事|こと}かけぬやうをはからひて{過|す}ぐる、{最上|さいじやう}のやうにてあるなり。
{一|ひとつ}{上臈|じやうらふ}は{下臈|げらふ}になり、{智者|ちしや}は{愚者|ぐしや}になり、{徳人|とくにん}は{貧|ひん}になり、{能|のう}ある{人|ひと}は{無能|むのう}になるべきなり。
{一|ひとつ}{仏道|ぶつだう}を{願|ねが}ふといふは、{別|べつ}のこと{無|な}し、{暇|いとま}ある{身|み}になりて、{世|よ}のこと{心|こころ}にかけぬを、{第一|だいいち}の{道|みち}とす。
この{外|ほか}も、ありし{事|こと}ども、{覚|おぼ}えず。
literal: When I read a booklet that wrote down what venerable holy men had said and left behind, named Ichigon Hōdan or something like that, the things that agreed with my heart and that I remember:
Item: a thing about which one thinks 'Should I do it, or should I not?' is generally better not done.
Item: a person who thinks of the next life should not own even one jar of rice-bran paste.
Even down to the sutra one carries and one's image of the Buddha, to own good things is pointless.
Item: for one who has left the world, to get by arranging things so that one does not feel the lack of what one does not have is the best way.
Item: the high-ranking should become low-ranking, the wise should become foolish, the rich should become poor, and people with ability should become without ability.
Item: wishing for the Buddhist path is nothing else: to become a person with leisure and not to keep the affairs of the world in mind is taken as the first way.
Besides these there were other things, but I do not remember them.

notes.text: The Ichigon Hōdan, 'Fragrant Talks in a Word', a collection of short sayings by holy men of the Pure Land school, among them Hōnen (1133–1212). It was compiled in the Kamakura period; the compiler and the exact date are unknown. Kenkō's wording is not always the same as the surviving text. とかや: 'or something like that', a casual touch, as if he were not sure of the title.

notes.quote: 心に会ひて覚えし事ども
notes.text: 'Things that agreed with my heart and that I remembered'. The sentence has no verb at the end: it works as a heading for the list.
{一|ひとつ}: 'item', a list marker at the start of each entry, used in documents like a bullet point. や … まし: hesitation, 'should I…?'. The advice: when in doubt, don't.
{後世|ごせ}: the next life, after rebirth (see section 4). Modern {後世|こうせい} means 'later generations'.
{糂汰|じんだ}: rice-bran paste for pickling vegetables, today's ぬかみそ. A jar of it was about the plainest thing a household could own.

notes.quote: 持経、本尊にいたるまで
notes.text: {持経|ぢきやう}: the sutra a priest keeps and recites. {本尊|ほぞん}: the image of the Buddha he worships (modern ほんぞん). Even holy objects become possessions, if they are good ones.

{臈|らふ}: a year as a monk. A monk's rank depended on how many years he had been ordained, so {上臈|じやうらふ} were senior, high-ranking people and {下臈|げらふ} junior, low ones. The words were also used outside the temple.
{第一|だいいち}: 'first, most important'. The path is not some special practice: it is free time and a mind that is not busy with the world.

notes.quote: この外も、ありし事ども、覚えず
notes.text: The section ends flatly: there were more, and he has forgotten them.
